A positive integer with exactly four divisors must be either:

1. \(p^3\) for a prime \(p\), with divisor sum  
   \[
   1+p+p^2+p^3,
   \]
   or

2. \(pq\) for distinct primes \(p,q\), with divisor sum  
   \[
   1+p+q+pq=(p+1)(q+1).
   \]

First, check \(p^3\):
\[
1+11+11^2+11^3=1464<2010,\quad
1+13+13^2+13^3=2380>2019.
\]
So no \(p^3\) works.

Now we need
\[
n=(p+1)(q+1)
\]
for distinct primes \(p,q\), with \(2010\le n\le 2019\).

For distinct primes, this product is always even, so only check even candidates:
\[
2010,2012,2014,2016,2018.
